rows.title: Today · every error is the server's bare page
rows.note:
Seen on the shipped container (localhost:5173 runs the Docker stack, not the dev server).

• Any missing address shows nginx's own page: Times, white, "404 Not Found", a server version. No masthead, no way back.
• nginx is told to show /404.html, but the build never writes that file.
• There is no error page in the app at all, so a page that fails while loading shows the framework's default.
• Offline, signed out, no access and a section that fails have no designed state yet.

Yardstick: 0 of 7 error states designed; 0 ways back from a missing page.

rows.title: A · The check that ran
rows.note:
Bet: an error page is evidence, like the rest of Maester. It says what you asked for, what it checked and the closest real page, then lets you search every page that exists.

Play: the inked letter in /term[i]nal shows the typo; the search filters as you type (no motion). The trace rows resolve at 120ms steps on load, the index page's existing moment.

Motion rule: fully legal as written.

Cost: one +error.svelte, a route list, a closest-match function. The least playful.

rows.title: B · Squash and stretch
rows.note:
Bet: the play is in the type. The 404 is set in the font's width axis; drag it (or focus it and use the arrow keys) and it squeezes to 62% or stretches to 125%, with a ruler showing the real range. The sentence stays the h1; the number is the toy.

In the terminal the number is still and squeezed, never draggable.

Motion rule: legal. Dragging is direct manipulation with no duration; nothing animates on its own.

Cost: one slider-like component. No new tokens, no drawings. Without script it is a still number.

rows.title: C · The sketchbook
rows.note:
Bet: the sign-in sketches become a family. Each error gets a two-plate drawing in the same hand: an empty ledger under a magnifying glass that follows your pointer (404), a confused old computer (failed page), a cable you drag into a socket to check the connection again (offline).

In the terminal the drawing is small and still.

Motion rule: legal (pointer-driven). Drawings are unframed: the 30px radius stays on sign-in.

Cost: highest. About 5 drawings; the illustration inks spread to more pages.

rows.title: D · Reconcile while you wait
rows.note:
Bet: the play teaches the product. A 404 shows five synthetic holdings where one value has two digits swapped; pick it and the row inverts with the arithmetic. "Another one" gives a new round.

Never in the terminal: no puzzle next to real figures. Inside the shell D looks like A2.

Motion rule: legal (state snaps).

Cost: a puzzle component and copy that must stay true ("Synthetic example" on the table). Longest phone page: 1.3 screens.

rows.title: Every direction · the states with no play
rows.note:
These are the same in all four directions. The more is at stake, the less play: inside the terminal, nothing moves next to your figures.

S1 not found in the terminal · S2 signed out · S3 no access (details cleared) · S4 offline plus one section that didn't load (unknown shows as "—", never zero) · S5 the site itself down: a static page with no script.

Sign-in errors (wrong password, too many attempts, expired link, waitlist) are already specified in SIGN_IN.md on feat/sign-in and are not redrawn.

shared:
THE SCREEN SET (every direction)

1. Not found, public: the build writes 404.html; nginx already points at it.
2. Not found in the terminal: unknown terminal address, in the shell.
3. A page failed to load: the app's error page, any other status.
4. Offline: a banner when the connection drops; full page if a page can't load.
5. Signed out: back to sign-in, then to the page you were on.
6. No access: details cleared, way back to your overview.
7. One section failed: local note, try again, "—" for figures that need it.
8. Site down: a static 50x page nginx serves, no script.

SHARED FIXES
• The sentence is the h1; the code (404, 500) is secondary, in the rail.
• One primary action, visible and focusable before any play; play is never the first tab stop.
• Every play is optional, keyboard-operable and announced in a status line.
• Reduced motion: nothing changes, because nothing moves on its own.
• Errors never name a server, a code path or a framework.
questions:
OPEN QUESTIONS

1. How much play do you want? A word picks the letter: "none" → A, "type" → B, "drawings" → C, "a game" → D.

2. May error pages bend the motion rule (e.g. a short spring-back after a drag)? As drawn, nothing needs it.

3. Should the site-down page (S5) be built now? It needs an nginx change as well as the page.
